topic: Can simultaneous uplink/downlink beam reconfiguration cause interference in tightly packed Ku-band spectrum allocations?
consensus_response: Simultaneous uplink/downlink beam reconfiguration causes interference among tightly packed Ku-band spectrum allocations due to spatial overlap between beams, leading to inline and aggregate interference. The array factor of the satellite's antenna affects beam directionality and sidelobe levels, causing energy leakage into adjacent beams. This degrades the achievable SINR by up to 16.49 dBi, impacting communication links and overall system capacity.
reference_context: The reference context provides various studies on satellite communications, including interference management techniques such as precoding, resource allocation, and admission control. The studies highlight the importance of mitigating inline interference caused by adjacent beam sidelobe gains and suggest employing orthogonal polarizations to reduce frequency reuse efficiency.
